transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A Zanussi ZDT21006FA that trips your electrics is a safety hazard. Because this involves an electrical fault to earth, please do not keep resetting the breaker and running the machine; repeated tripping can indicate a worsening insulation failure that could become dangerous. The most common cause for a trip occurring partway through a cycle (around 15 minutes in) is a failing heater element or circulation pump where moisture has compromised the electrical insulation, causing it to 'leak' current to earth when under load. Less commonly, it could be an issue with the mains filter inside the machine or wiring that chafes. To narrow this down safely, I need to know exactly when the trip happens:
1. Does it trip the moment you switch the socket on (before the door is even opened)?
2. Or does it only trip once the programme has started and the machine begins washing or heating? Please let me know which of these matches your experience.
It doesn't trip when I switch it on, only once a wash is running, usually 10-20 mins in on the 65C programme. It's on the same circuit as my fridge, so that's a worry too.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
That timing—10–20 minutes into a hot wash—is classic for an electrical fault that appears only when the heating element is under load. At this stage, the machine has filled with water and is trying to heat it; if the insulation inside the heater element has degraded (often due to limescale or age), current can 'leak' through the metal casing into the earth wire, tripping your RCD. The circulation pump is another possibility, but the timing points to the heater first. To confirm this safely, please:
1. Switch off and unplug the dishwasher at the wall socket.
2. Remove the bottom kickplate (usually held by a few screws or clips) to expose the base of the machine.
3. Locate the heater element (a metal disc or loop at the back/bottom of the tub).
4. Disconnect the two electrical wires from the heater terminals.
5. Using a multimeter set to resistance (Ohms), measure between each terminal and the bare metal body of the heater. If you get a reading (continuity) between any terminal and the metal casing, the element is faulty and leaking current to earth. This suggests the cause. If there is no continuity (infinite resistance/O.L.), the heater is likely okay, and we should look at the circulation pump or wiring next. Please let me know what the multimeter shows, or if you are not comfortable doing this test.
Sorry, I won't take the kickplate off, and I don't have a multimeter or insulation tester anyway. Is there anything else I can safely check, or should I get an engineer in?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
And because this is an active electrical safety hazard (the appliance is leaking current to earth), you should not use it again. Do not try to bypass the trip or reset the breaker repeatedly. The most likely cause is a failing heating element where moisture has compromised its insulation, causing it to leak electricity when it tries to heat the water around 15 minutes into the cycle. A less common possibility is a similar fault in the circulation pump or internal wiring. Please arrange for a qualified appliance engineer to inspect and repair the machine before using it again.

candidates: Circulation pump or drain pump leakage (medium)
Mains filter or incoming wiring fault (low)
